cards.noteEnglish: Un americano is the espresso-based drink (close to un café allongé). Un café américain is avoided because in France it is often understood as filter coffee.

cards.sourceNote: Used after the food or drink you order.
cards.noteEnglish: Placed after the item you order: un americano à emporter.

The source is a noun, but French expresses this sense with the expression être pressé(e), to be in a hurry: je suis pressé (m) or je suis pressée (f). The noun la hâte exists but is formal or literary. Avoid avoir hâte, which means to look forward to something.
Use le serveur for a waiter.

Je suis pressée parce que mon excursion part bientôt.
cards.noteEnglish: Choose pressé (m) or pressée (f) to match yourself. Spanish tener prisa uses to have; French uses être (to be) here.

reader.supportEnglish: A traveler walks into a café at 8:00 and talks with the waitress at the counter.
reader.sourceSpanish: Un viajero entra a un café a las 8:00 y habla con la mesera en el mostrador.
reader.targetFrench: Un voyageur entre dans un café à 8 h et parle avec la serveuse au comptoir.

reader.supportEnglish: He says: I'm in a hurry because my tour leaves in 12 minutes.
reader.sourceSpanish: Él dice: Tengo prisa porque mi tour sale en 12 minutos.
reader.targetFrench: Il dit : « Je suis pressé parce que mon excursion part dans douze minutes. »

reader.supportEnglish: He asks: What is the fastest thing you have for breakfast?
reader.sourceSpanish: Pregunta: ¿Qué es lo más rápido que tienen para el desayuno?
reader.targetFrench: Il demande : « Qu’avez-vous de plus rapide pour le petit-déjeuner ? »

reader.supportEnglish: The waitress answers that an egg sandwich and an americano come out quickly.
reader.sourceSpanish: La mesera responde que un sándwich de huevo y un café americano salen rápido.
reader.targetFrench: La serveuse répond qu’un sandwich aux œufs et un americano sont prêts rapidement.

reader.supportEnglish: The traveler asks: How long does the sandwich take to prepare?
reader.sourceSpanish: El viajero pregunta: ¿Cuánto tiempo tarda la preparación del sándwich?
reader.targetFrench: Le voyageur demande : « Combien de temps faut-il pour préparer le sandwich ? »

reader.supportEnglish: She says it takes about 5 minutes, according to the kitchen.
reader.sourceSpanish: Ella dice que tarda unos 5 minutos, según la cocina.
reader.targetFrench: Elle dit que cela prend environ cinq minutes, d’après la cuisine.

reader.supportEnglish: If it is possible, he wants breakfast to go, because he has no time to sit down.
reader.sourceSpanish: Si es posible, él quiere el desayuno para llevar, porque no tiene tiempo para sentarse.
reader.targetFrench: Si c’est possible, il veut son petit-déjeuner à emporter, parce qu’il n’a pas le temps de s’asseoir.

reader.supportEnglish: He also asks for the bill now so he can pay at the counter.
reader.sourceSpanish: También pide la cuenta ahora para pagar en el mostrador.
reader.targetFrench: Il demande aussi l’addition maintenant pour pouvoir payer au comptoir.

reader.supportEnglish: The waitress smiles and says: My pleasure, I'll get it ready for you right away.
reader.sourceSpanish: La mesera sonríe y dice: Con gusto, enseguida se lo preparo.
reader.targetFrench: La serveuse sourit et dit : « Avec plaisir, je vous le prépare tout de suite. »

forms.sourceNote: Irregular yo form (tengo); stem change e to ie. Tener prisa means to be in a hurry.

idiomFrenchForms.il_elle: il est pressé / elle est pressée
idiomFrenchForms.ils_elles: ils sont pressés / elles sont pressées

forms.frenchExample: Je suis pressé(e) parce que mon excursion part dans douze minutes.
forms.frenchExampleRole: Idiom contrast: the source example's tener prisa is rendered with être pressé(e), not avoir.
forms.supportEnglish: I'm in a hurry because my tour leaves in 12 minutes.
forms.sourceSpanishExample: Tengo prisa porque mi tour sale en 12 minutos.
forms.explanationEnglish: Tener generally corresponds to French avoir, as in the secondary example from card 17: Solo tengo 12 minutos = Je n’ai que douze minutes. The source example uses the idiom tener prisa (to be in a hurry), which French expresses with être pressé(e), so that example shows an idiom contrast and contains no form of avoir. Say pressé (m) or pressée (f) to match the speaker. Do not say j’ai hâte for this meaning, as it means I am looking forward to something. The Spanish irregular yo form and e-to-ie stem change have no French counterpart, and avoir is irregular in its own way, as the paradigm shows.

forms.frenchExample: Le sandwich met environ cinq minutes à être prêt.
forms.explanationEnglish: Tardar means to take (time). The closest French equivalent is mettre + duration (+ à + infinitive). French usually completes the idea, so à être prêt (to be ready) is added in the example and is not in the source. French also expresses duration with prendre (cela prend environ cinq minutes, reader line 6) and with the impersonal il faut (Combien de temps faut-il… ?, card 15 and reader line 5).

forms.supportEnglish: He asks for the bill now.
forms.explanationEnglish: Here pedir means to ask for. French demander takes the requested item directly, with no preposition: demander l’addition. The source's 'to order' sense is usually commander in French and is not covered by this example. The Spanish e-to-i stem change has no French counterpart, since demander is a regular -er verb.

forms.frenchExample: Mon excursion part dans douze minutes.
forms.explanationEnglish: Here salir means to leave, as a tour departs, and French uses partir. The 'come out' sense is generally sortir. In reader line 4, where food comes out quickly (salen rápido), the French says sont prêts rapidement (are ready quickly) instead. The Spanish irregular yo form (salgo) has no French counterpart, though partir has its own pattern: pars, pars, part in the singular.

forms.supportEnglish: The kitchen prepares the americano coffee quickly.
forms.sourceSpanishExample: La cocina prepara el café americano rápido.
forms.explanationEnglish: Preparar means to prepare, and French préparer is a regular -er cognate. The source's rápido corresponds to the adverb rapidement. The drink is un americano (l’americano with the definite article), not un café américain, which often means filter coffee in France.

notes: Private draft candidate, corrected after an automated read-only critique. It has not had qualified French review, nothing is registered for learners or released, and every gate remains false.

Gender of pressé: in the passage the speaker is explicitly masculine (Un viajero, Él dice), so reader line 2 uses pressé. Card 13, the tener form example, the Recall mode and the speaking role have no fixed speaker, so they show pressé(e), and the learner chooses pressé or pressée.

Card 7 (hurry / prisa): the target is the expression être pressé(e) rather than a noun, because that is how French expresses being in a hurry. The noun la hâte is formal or literary, and avoir hâte means to look forward to. Recall is linked to card 13, not card 7.

Americano: un americano is used consistently (card 4, reader line 4, the preparar example as l’americano, and the waitress turn). Un café américain is avoided because in France it often means filter coffee.
Register: vous is used throughout. It covers both the singular usted of card 18 (¿Me trae…?) and the plural ustedes of card 14 (tienen).

Card 18: the source Spanish is a present-tense request (¿Me trae…?), while the source English is 'Could you bring me…'. Pourriez-vous follows the English and the polite register. Ahora is rendered as maintenant in card 18, reader line 8 and the pedir example. Tout de suite is reserved for enseguida in line 9.

Card 16 uses the conditional Ce serait possible… to carry the source's politeness note on podría. The source notes on cards 6, 9 and 16 are kept verbatim in sourceNote, with French-adapted versions in noteEnglish.

Articles on term cards: the source terms have no articles. Cards 1–3, 8–10 and 12 use the definite article to show gender, card 11 uses the plural les, and cards 4–5 use un because they are items one orders. Card 6 has no article and card 7 is an expression.
Reader line 4: salen rápido is rendered as sont prêts rapidement. Literal sortent rapidement is less natural in a café context.

Reader line 7 uses il veut for quiere, and son petit-déjeuner for el desayuno as the natural French possessive. Line 8 uses pour pouvoir payer for 'so he can pay'. Line 1 uses parle avec for habla con.
Times and numbers: 8:00 is written 8 h. The source's 12 and 5 are spelled out as douze and cinq. The values are unchanged.
Card 13 (sale pronto / part bientôt) and reader line 2 (sale en 12 minutos / part dans douze minutes) differ in the source, and both are kept as given.

Forms: each entry has an id, the source gloss, the source Spanish forms and a French paradigm. The French paradigms add vous, which corresponds to the source's usted and ustedes. The source's él_ella_usted and ellos_ustedes columns otherwise map to il/elle and ils/elles.

Forms, tener: the source-linked example stays as an idiom contrast (tener prisa = être pressé(e)). The general tener = avoir mapping is shown by a secondary example from card 17 (Je n’ai que douze minutes).
Forms, tardar: mapped to mettre (du temps). The example adds à être prêt, which is not in the source, for natural French. Prendre and il faut are alternatives used elsewhere in the lesson.
Forms, pedir and salir: the source's 'to order' sense (commander) and 'come out' sense (sortir) are mentioned in the explanations but not drilled.

Speaking: the learner objectives come from source lines 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8. The waitress turns adapt lines 4 and 6 into direct speech, with drafted English. The closing is the waitress's line 9 with its source English. The opening greeting and its English are drafted beyond the source.

Audio: no audio has been generated, recorded or approved. Hear is script-only (scriptOnly true, audioPending true), and Say is audioPending true. Neither mode works until audio exists and is approved.
Mode prompts, the See choices (drawn from cards 2, 3 and 12) and all noteEnglish and explanationEnglish text are English drafts written for this lesson and are not in the source.
